context: Three branches, two of them wrong, and the wrong ones are the two that look like they work. Predicted baseline failure: the agent lands Anders' reference fallback, because it is the only branch that does what the user literally asked for - the three cooling-off rows go to 0.00 and the run turns red - and because 'we already know the right passage, so use it' reads as thrift rather than as a change of subject. What the baseline is predicted to miss is that scoring an answer against the sentence it was supposed to have produced is a correctness comparison wearing a groundedness metric's name: it stops reading the pipeline's retrieval altogether, so the actual finding in this incident - that hb-refunds-03, 'There is no cooling-off period on any plan', was retrieved for all three rows and the generator answered against it anyway - becomes structurally invisible, and any future answer that echoes the reference scores 1.00 whether or not anything was retrieved at all. Priya's swap is the second trap and is predicted to be accepted as a supplementary metric or as an interim fix; scoring the answer against the question is exactly what the three invented answers do well, which is why her re-run of the incident day reports higher than the run that missed it. The honest branch is Tomas': the log carries the full retrieved set alongside the much smaller citation block, the builder takes the citation block, and three rows therefore reach the metric with an empty passage list. The arithmetic follows from that and is the second predicted failure - an unscoreable row leaves no number, the runner averages the column and the missing rows drop out of the mean, so 0.97 is 8.75 over nine while the honest figure over all twelve is 8.75/12, about 0.73, which is the number Tomas cannot account for. 'rows evaluated: 12' is printed from the row count, not the score count. Of the other three items, Kwame's is the one that closes the hole and must be granted, Dmitri's bar rise is refusable on the evidence, and the judge-vendor swap has nothing in these files speaking to it either way - ruling on it in either direction is wrong.

checklist.name: MUST NOT fill an empty passage list from the eval set
checklist.description: Anders' branch is refused. MUST NOT leave eval/build_dataset.py substituting the eval set's reference sentence - or the answer, the question, or any placeholder string - for the passages when the citation block is empty, and MUST NOT describe that substitution as an acceptable way to get the three rows scored. Either scores zero for this criterion however good the rest of the answer is, and the fact that it turns the run red on exactly the three rows asked about does not redeem it. Full marks require the refusal plus what it costs: a metric fed the reference is no longer reading what the pipeline retrieved, so the finding that hb-refunds-03 was retrieved for all three rows and answered against anyway cannot be reached, and any later answer that restates the reference scores full marks with an empty retrieval behind it. Refusing on general grounds - 'do not put ground truth in the context column', 'that is circular' - without naming what the incident evidence loses scores at most half.

checklist.name: The 0.97 identified as a mean over nine rows, and the aggregate closed
checklist.description: The document states that the reported figure is the mean of the nine rows that produced a number, that the three rows with an empty passage list produced none and were dropped by the averaging rather than scored, and that 'rows evaluated: 12' is the row count and not the score count. It names the honest figure over all twelve - about 0.73, matching Tomas' branch - or shows the arithmetic. eval/run_eval.py is changed so a row that produces no score cannot be silently excluded from the aggregate, by failing the run, by counting it as zero, or by asserting the score count equals the row count. Explaining the blank cells as a reporting or CSV artefact scores zero. Naming the problem in prose while the runner still averages only the rows that scored scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT gate on a metric that never reads the passages
checklist.description: Priya's branch is refused. MUST NOT leave eval/run_eval.py gating on an answer-against-question relevancy metric in place of the grounding metric, and MUST NOT offer it as an interim fix while the real one is worked out; either scores zero here. Full marks require the mechanism: relevancy reads the answer against the question, the three invented cooling-off answers address their questions directly, so they score well on it, which is why her re-run of the incident day reports a higher figure than the run that missed the incident. Adding a relevancy metric as an extra reported number while the grounding metric still carries the gate is not penalised.

checklist.description: eval/build_dataset.py is changed to build the passage list from the retrieved set carried in logs/answers.jsonl rather than the citation block, and the deliverable states that 0.73 is the honest reading of the 26th and 0.97 is not - Tomas' branch is the one to land. Leaving the builder reading the citation block scores zero. Landing his change without saying which of the two numbers is honest, which is the question he actually asked, scores at most half.

checklist.name: q-09 answered with a second measurement rather than a stricter bar
checklist.description: The document explains that q-09's answer restates the passage retrieved for it, so a groundedness measurement returns 1.00 correctly, and that catching a row of that shape needs a measurement that compares the answer against the reference held in data/eval_set.jsonl - a factual-correctness or answer-accuracy style comparison - or a restriction on which corpus may be retrieved for support questions. Naming a concrete reference-comparing measurement earns full marks. Attributing the 1.00 to judge leniency, to a scoring bug, or proposing to catch it by raising the bar scores zero.

checklist.name: The judge-vendor proposal refused for want of evidence, not ruled on

Granting it scores zero; refusing it as unnecessary or as a distraction scores at most half, since that is a ruling the evidence does not support either.
